title: Gokaldas Exports Ltd - 532630 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Gokaldas Q1 FY27: consolidated income up 21% YoY and EBITDA up 17%, with Africa up 45% and India up 16% amid a sector-wide 12% decline.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as a strong, broad-based quarter, with consolidated income up 21% YoY and consolidated EBITDA up 17% (India EBITDA up 14%). India revenue grew 16% YoY against a 12% fall in Indian apparel exports, partly helped by the lower US tariff regime. Africa grew 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak prior-year base, but Africa EBITDA margin was about 8%, below normal. Cost pressures from wages (Haryana minimum wage up 35% from April 2026), fuel, chemicals, logistics and freight were significant, partly offset by overhead control and a weaker rupee. BTPL (fabric unit) remains loss-making at the operating level, with merger expected in Q3 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Target: double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28

financial_highlights.metric: India wage cost increase in Q1
Other expenses cost hit (utilities and logistics)

financial_highlights.change: Mix-driven; management disputed the volume metric

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 14%, versus a 12% decline in Indian apparel exports. Matrix plus stand-alone India ASP cited at INR 613 with about 1.53 million pieces for the old Gurgaon units. Central India plants running at about 85% utilisation; South India plants full.

segments.name: Africa
segments.commentary: Revenue up 45% YoY on AGOA renewal and a weak Q1 FY26 base. EBITDA margin about 8%, with management targeting double-digit by Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Utilisation at 80-85%; FY27 visibility of USD 112-115 million against a USD 120 million target.

segments.name: BTPL (fabric unit)
segments.commentary: Running at 50-53 lakh meters per month, with Q1 turnover around INR 170 crore and operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%. Targets EBITDA break-even in H1, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Growth: management said 15%-plus growth is 'straightforward' and it should do better; mid-to-high-teens was floated by the analyst, with management not confirming a number. Q2 FY27 revenue expected to resemble Q1; Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked.
Africa FY27 revenue visibility of USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, with a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.
Africa EBITDA margin expected back to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28.
ETR guided at 20-22% for FY27 as international operations contribute.
Wage, fuel and logistics cost pressure expected to partly ease in H2 if conditions improve; uncertainty remains. Pass-through pricing being applied to new orders.

Capex: about INR 80 crore mentioned in presentation; Jharkhand and Karnataka greenfield units total about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27), with steady-state revenue of about INR 350 crore from FY29. Bhopal second unit yields revenue from H2 FY27.
Potential 2,000-3,000 extra machines (about INR 200 crore revenue per 1,000 machines) to be decided within 3 months; larger spend in FY28.
capex_capacity: Bhopal second unit ramping up, expected to reach near full utilisation by Q4 FY27; adds about 3.5 million pieces and about INR 175-200 crore steady-state revenue.

Karnataka and Ranchi existing-factory machine additions (about 500-700 machines) are being commissioned in FY27; total of commissioned Bhopal Phase 2, Karnataka and Ranchi adds about INR 275 crore revenue potential.

New Jharkhand and Karnataka facilities: total investment about INR 100 crore, about 3.5 million pieces each, steady-state revenue about INR 350 crore combined; expected on stream H2 FY28, full potential FY29.
Africa: capacity already in place to deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue; second shift used for swing capacity; no significant Africa capex planned until existing options are exhausted.
BTPL capacity about 50 lakh meters per month, expected to grow about 30%; new customer onboarding with operations starting in Q2.
demand_pricing: US and UK end-consumer demand grew strongly through the first six months of CY26, though US growth slowed in June; EU and UK apparel imports declined through the first five months of FY27 per management.
US Section 301 tariff places India on par with competing sourcing countries, while China and Vietnam face 12.5%. India-UK FTA brings parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam in the UK.
Management says European buyers and US buyers are increasing inquiries and business towards India, extending beyond fashion and outerwear into shirts and bottoms; denim inquiries also rising.
Pricing: fabric cost pass-through is standard; some items (poly bags, cartons, fuel) were not priced into Q1 orders set in January and will be priced going forward.
Product mix: ASPs range from about USD 40-50 for high-value products to lower-value items; average realisation in India about INR 613 per piece for Gurgaon units.
UK is about 4-4.5% of total revenue; focus on larger UK players such as Marks & Spencer. Fibre mix about 65% cotton and up to 30% man-made (annual).

qa_highlights.question: India volume growth was only 3.4%, so where does India volume go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is a misleading metric because Q1 and Q2 are high-value outerwear with 150-250 minutes of content per garment, versus about 22-25 minutes for a shirt; it added there is no YoY volume drop and growth is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Does the strong order book mean the mid-teens growth guide holds, or can growth be mid-to-high teens?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Spring '27 orders execute in Q3 FY27 and revenue traction for that period and beyond looks similar to Q1; 15%-plus growth was called 'straightforward' and it should do better.

qa_highlights.question: When will Africa EBITDA margin recover to double digits from about 8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28, with H2 the differentiator; it cited AGOA expiring December with a 2-year extension passed by the Senate and awaiting the House and presidential assent.

qa_highlights.question: What is the visibility on shipping delays, and could they delay orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is the worst shipping environment; outbound FOB shipments can wait about 2 weeks for a vessel, and it expects easing over the next two quarters as the war and typhoon issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: How do India incentive cuts (RoSCTL) and the BTPL merger affect margins, and is the Africa margin base higher?
qa_highlights.answer: RoSCTL is about 3.5% and management's worst case is a halving to about 1.75%, which it expects to offset; BTPL should reach mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA after merger in Q3. Management said the EBITDA margin would be a bit higher than the analyst's base, and it sees the rupee weakness as a cushion (about 70% of dollars hedged at about INR 89).

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q2 and H2 visibility, particularly for India?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 and Q2 are booked; Q2 revenue should look like Q1. Q3 and Q4 orders are being booked now and the projection looks good despite US inflation concerns.

qa_highlights.question: Is India gaining share from China and Vietnam after the tariff change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2.5% advantage is not remarkable by itself, but European and US buyers are increasing inquiries for India across shirts, bottoms and denim, not just fashion and outerwear.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 35% minimum wage hike a larger hit, and how is it being handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Haryana minimum wage rose 35% from April 2026 but overall wages for the Gurgaon/Manesar units rose only 14-15%; India wage cost increase in Q1 was about INR 20 crore, absorbed in the system. Karnataka increase was about 5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other expenses increase and the ETR outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose by about INR 5-6 crore on utilities, gas, fuel and chemicals plus inbound and outbound logistics, partly expected to ease in H2; FY27 ETR is guided at 20-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BTPL Q1 performance and the break-even timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: BTPL had about INR 170 crore fabric turnover in Q1 with operational EBITDA of about -7.5% to -8%; management targets EBITDA break-even in H1 (Q2), EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex and capacity plan, including Jharkhand, Karnataka and Bhopal?
qa_highlights.answer: Jharkhand and Karnataka together need about INR 100 crore (INR 70-75 crore in FY27) for about INR 350 crore steady-state revenue, coming on stream H2 FY28; Bhopal Phase 2 adds about 3.5 million pieces and INR 175-200 crore revenue. Management also said it may add 2,000-3,000 machines with a decision within 3 months and larger spend in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Africa plan require more capex, and what is the Africa capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: No significant Africa capex is planned until second-shift options are exhausted; capacity in place can deliver about USD 120 million annual revenue. FY27 visibility is USD 112-115 million against the USD 120 million target, a quarterly run-rate of about USD 30 million.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Indian business share, utilisation and product-wise breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Central India plants run about 85% utilisation and South India plants are full; Africa is at 80-85%. Management gave the old Gurgaon units at 1.53 million pieces at INR 613 ASP, while Matrix alone was about 1.5 million pieces at INR 613.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric mix and UK exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton is about 65% or a little higher and man-made fibres up to 30%, on an annual basis per management. UK is about 4-4.5% of revenue, with focus on larger players such as Marks & Spencer.

risks_watch: Africa EBITDA margin (about 8% in Q1) must recover to double-digit in Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28; AGOA expires December 2026 and the extension is still awaiting House and presidential approval.
Shipping and logistics: container shortages, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea disruption, and typhoon-related sailing delays; FOB outbound goods can sit about 2 weeks before boarding.
Wage and cost inflation: Haryana minimum wage up 35%, RoSCTL at about 3.5% with a possible halving to 1.75%, plus fuel, chemicals and poly bag/carton costs not priced into Q1 orders.
BTPL execution: operational EBITDA about -7.5% to -8% in Q1; break-even in Q2, EBITDA positive in Q3 and PBT positive in Q4 FY27; merger expected in Q3 FY27.
India volume metric disputed (3.4% per analyst), with growth attributed to mix; Q2 revenue expected to be similar to Q1, and Q3/Q4 orders still being booked.
Demand: US import growth slowed in June, EU and UK apparel imports declined, and US inflation could affect retail demand.

summary.management_tone: Confident and broadly upbeat on growth, order book and tariff positioning, but cautious on margins, shipping costs, AGOA beyond December and policy items such as RoSCTL and minimum wages, where management repeatedly declined to give numbers.
